data.name: Ashavin
data.gender_notes: Ashavin is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ashavin is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Asa' meaning 'Love' and 'Vin' meaning 'Protection'. He is a God worshipped for love, protection, and wisdom. Ashavin is also known as the god of love and is believed to be the protector of lovers. The name Ashavin carries the meaning “God of Love and Protection” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Ashavin usually hope their child will grow to embody god of love and protection and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine love and protection of the universe.
data.etymology: Ashavin belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Love and Protection.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ashavin total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: Hanuman Chalisa, a 40-line hymn in Devanagari script, extols the virtues of Hanuman, the monkey god. It is popular amongst Hindus and Jains, and has been set to various tunes and rendered as devotional songs across India. Hanuman, the embodiment of monkey power, strength, courage, and wisdom, is widely revered for his unwavering devotion to Rama and Sita.
data.spiritual_significance: Hanuman is considered a human form of the 'Maruts', the divine wind gods, who can traverse the skies and shape the elements. He is revered as a manifestation of Shiva and a representative of the power of devotion or 'Bhakti'. A spectacle of divine strength and unwavering commitment to his Lord, Hanuman remains an eternal symbol of selfless love and devotion.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ashavin is a name derived from Lord Ashvin, the divine healer in Hindu mythology. It symbolizes healing, rejuvenation, and protection. The name Ashavin evokes the power of Lord Ashvin's blessings for physical and spiritual well-being.
